label: Java Backend (Fresher)
blurb: Java backend interview prep for 0–2 YOE: core Java, OOP, collections, Spring Boot basics, SQL, REST APIs, DSA, Git, and behavioral questions that come up in fresher and first-job interviews.
audience: 0–2 YOE Java developers, fresh graduates, bootcamp completers

modules.title: Java Syntax & Language Fundamentals
modules.intro: Java syntax (fresher level) introduces the language fundamentals. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with data types and variables (the primitives and references), then operators and control flow (the logic), then arrays. Type casting and access modifiers follow at the mechanics tier, then keywords and literals. It closes with the comparisons topic.

modules.title: Java OOP Fundamentals
modules.intro: Java OOP (fresher level) introduces object-oriented programming. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with classes and objects (the starting point), then the four pillars — encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction — in the order a fresher learns them. Constructors and this/super follow at the mechanics tier, then the interfaces-vs-abstract-classes question (the #1 OOP comparison). It closes with the comparisons topic.

modules.title: Java Strings & Wrapper Classes
modules.intro: Java Strings (fresher level) introduces the most-used class. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with String immutability (why Strings can't change — the foundation), then the string pool (the memory optimization that follows from immutability). String methods and comparisons follow, then StringBuilder vs StringBuffer (the mutable companions). String programs are the applied tier, then autoboxing/unboxing and wrapper classes — the primitives-to-objects bridge that pairs with String questions.

modules.title: Java Collections Framework
modules.intro: Java Collections (fresher level) introduces the framework a junior uses every day. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the collection hierarchy (the interface tree) and generics (the type safety that makes collections usable), then the three interface families — List, Set, Map — and their implementations. The famous comparisons (ArrayList vs LinkedList, HashMap internals, HashSet vs TreeSet) follow at the canon tier, then iteration and the comparison topic.

modules.title: Java Exception Handling
modules.intro: Java exceptions (fresher level) introduces the error-handling model. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the exception hierarchy (Throwable → Error/Exception → RuntimeException), then checked vs unchecked (the debate every fresher must understand). Try-catch-finally and throw/throws follow at the mechanics tier, then try-with-resources (the modern cleanup pattern). Custom exceptions and common runtime exceptions are the applied tier, then exception best practices close the module.

modules.title: Java Multithreading Basics
modules.intro: Java multithreading (fresher level) introduces concurrency. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with thread basics and the lifecycle (NEW → RUNNABLE → TERMINATED), then creating threads and thread vs Runnable. Synchronization follows at the mechanics tier, then the concurrency problems (race conditions, deadlock) a fresher must recognize. The volatile keyword and wait/notify close the module at the coordination tier.

modules.title: Java 8 Features for Freshers
modules.intro: Java 8 features (fresher level) introduces the modern Java style. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with lambda expressions (the syntax revolution), then functional interfaces (the SAM types lambdas target) and method references. Streams follow — the centerpiece — split into basics and operations. Optional (the null-handling companion) and default/static interface methods close the feature tier, then comparisons.

modules.title: Java I/O & File Handling Basics
modules.intro: Java I/O (fresher level) introduces reading and writing. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the File class (the file-system entry point), then the two stream families — byte and character — and buffering (the performance layer). Stream types follow, then NIO (Path, Files — the modern API). Serialization and try-with-resources close the module at the applied tier.

modules.title: Spring Boot for Freshers
modules.intro: Spring Boot (fresher level) introduces the framework most Java backends use. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with what Spring Boot is and Spring vs Spring Boot (the convention-over-configuration revolution). Starters and auto-configuration follow at the mechanics tier, then component scan and the embedded server. REST controller basics and application.properties close the module at the applied tier.

modules.title: Spring Core & Dependency Injection
modules.intro: Spring Core and DI (fresher level) introduces the IoC container. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the IoC container (the core idea — inversion of control), then dependency injection and the DI types (constructor, setter, field). @Autowired and component annotations follow at the mechanics tier, then bean definitions and scopes. The Spring annotations overview closes the module.

modules.title: Spring Data JPA Basics
modules.intro: Spring Data JPA (fresher level) introduces ORM in Spring. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with JPA basics (the standard) and Hibernate basics (the implementation). Entity annotations and relationships follow at the modeling tier, then the repository layer — CRUD repository, JpaRepository, and derived query methods. Lazy vs eager loading closes the module at the performance tier.

modules.title: SQL Fundamentals
modules.intro: SQL fundamentals (fresher level) introduces the query language. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with SELECT (the starting query) and WHERE (filtering), then the SQL command families (DDL/DML/DQL). Constraints and joins follow at the structure tier, then GROUP BY/HAVING, subqueries, and aggregates. Indexes close the module at the performance tier, then comparisons.

modules.title: JDBC Fundamentals
modules.intro: JDBC (fresher level) introduces database access in Java. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with JDBC overview (what it is, the driver model), then the connection and statement types (Statement vs PreparedStatement — the security distinction). Result sets and connection pooling follow at the mechanics tier, then SQL injection (the vulnerability PreparedStatement prevents). It closes with JDBC vs JPA — the comparison that explains why JPA exists.

modules.title: Database Design Basics
modules.intro: Database design is the fresher-junior data foundation. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with ER diagrams (the modeling starting point), then keys (primary, foreign — the relational glue), then normalization (1NF-2NF-3NF — why we split tables). Transactions and ACID follow as the correctness tier, then the comparison tier — relational vs NoSQL and database comparisons — where a fresher learns when to choose what.

modules.title: REST API Fundamentals
modules.intro: REST API (fresher level) introduces web APIs. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with what REST is and the constraints (the architectural style), then HTTP methods and status codes (the verbs and responses). JSON and API design basics follow at the mechanics tier, then idempotency (the property interviewers test). It closes with REST vs SOAP — the comparison that explains why REST won.

modules.title: Spring MVC & REST Controllers
modules.intro: Spring MVC and REST (fresher level) introduces building web endpoints in Spring. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the MVC pattern and the DispatcherServlet (the front controller — the request lifecycle). @RestController and the request/response annotations follow at the mechanics tier, then path variables, ResponseEntity, and exception handling. Content negotiation closes the module at the advanced tier.

modules.title: SOLID & OOP Design Principles
modules.intro: Design principles (fresher level) introduces the SOLID set and the heuristics around it. This module is an elevation arc: it walks SOLID in order — SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP — so a fresher meets each principle and its failure mode. Then the two composition principles (composition vs inheritance, coupling and cohesion) that translate SOLID into daily class design. It closes with DRY-KISS-YAGNI — the pragmatics that keep a fresher from over-engineering.

modules.title: Design Patterns Introduction
modules.intro: Design patterns (fresher level) introduces the GoF patterns a junior should know. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the patterns overview (what patterns are, why they exist), then the creational patterns (singleton, factory, builder), then structural (decorator) and behavioral (observer, strategy). It closes with when-to-use-patterns — the judgment tier that stops a fresher from pattern-spamming.

modules.title: Low-Level Design (LLD) Basics
modules.intro: Low-level design (fresher level) introduces object-oriented design interviews. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the LLD approach and identifying classes (the method), then UML class diagrams (the notation). LLD interview strategy follows, then the classic fresher problems in order of difficulty — parking lot, library management, online shopping, and ATM design.

modules.title: Data Structures & Algorithms for Interviews
modules.intro: DSA fundamentals (fresher level) covers the data structures and algorithms a junior interview expects. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with complexity analysis (Big-O — the language every following answer is written in), then the linear structures (arrays, strings, linked lists, stacks, queues). Hashing follows (the enabler of O(1) interview solutions), then sorting, binary search, and trees — the structures that close the fresher DSA canon.

modules.title: Interview Problem-Solving Patterns
modules.intro: Problem-solving patterns (fresher level) introduces the DSA patterns a junior interview expects. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with the interview-approach framework (how to attack a problem), then recursion (the foundation for several patterns). Frequency counting, two pointers, and sliding window follow as the core patterns, then backtracking and dynamic programming intros at the advanced tier. Common fresher programs close the module.

modules.title: Web Security for Freshers
modules.intro: Web security (fresher level) introduces the threats every web developer must know. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with authentication vs authorization (the two concerns), then HTTPS and TLS (the transport security), then password hashing (the storage security). The injection family — SQL injection and XSS — follows at the attack tier, then CSRF. JWT and the OWASP Top 10 overview close the module at the awareness tier.

modules.title: JUnit 5 & Unit Testing
modules.intro: JUnit testing (fresher level) introduces automated testing. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with why unit testing (the motivation — defects, design, confidence), then JUnit 5 basics (the architecture), then annotations and lifecycle (the test hooks). Assertions and test naming follow at the mechanics tier, then parameterized tests (the data-driven pattern). Testing best practices close the module.

modules.title: Mockito & Test Doubles
modules.intro: Mockito (fresher level) introduces mocking for unit tests. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with what mocking is (the motivation — isolating the unit under test), then Mockito setup and the when/thenReturn stubbing pattern. Verify (the interaction assertion) and argument matchers follow at the mechanics tier, then mock vs stub vs spy (the test-double taxonomy). InjectMocks and testing Spring services close the module at the applied tier.

modules.title: Git Version Control
modules.intro: Git (fresher level) introduces version control a junior uses daily. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with Git basics (the model — commits, the DAG), then staging and committing (the daily loop), then branching. Remote repos and merging/rebasing follow, then the pain points a fresher hits — conflicts and pull requests. Git workflow closes the module at the team-collaboration tier.

modules.title: Maven & Gradle Build Tools
modules.intro: Maven and Gradle (fresher level) introduces Java build tools. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with what a build tool is (the motivation), then Maven (the dominant tool — overview, lifecycle, POM, dependency management, profiles). The Maven vs Gradle comparison follows, then running Spring Boot with Maven — the applied tier where the build tool meets the framework.

modules.title: Docker & Cloud Concepts Introduction
modules.intro: Docker and cloud (fresher level) introduces the deployment concepts a junior backend developer meets. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with what Docker is and the container-vs-VM distinction, then the image-vs-container model and Dockerfiles. Docker commands follow at the applied tier, then the cloud tier — cloud concepts, SaaS/PaaS/IaaS, and microservices as the architecture these tools enable.

modules.title: Debugging, Logging & Code Quality
modules.intro: Debugging and logging are the fresher survival skills. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with logging (the overview, the levels, SLF4J and Logback — the stack you'll use), then reading stack traces and common exceptions (the diagnosis skills). Debugging techniques and the IDE debugger follow at the applied tier, then code review basics — where a fresher learns to catch bugs before they ship.

modules.title: Fresher Behavioral & HR Questions
modules.intro: Fresher behavioral and HR rounds test communication, not experience. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with 'tell me about yourself' (the opener every interview starts with), then the motivation questions (why Java backend, why this company). Strengths and weaknesses and career goals follow, then the technical-behavioral bridge — project discussion. Teamwork and conflict are the interpersonal tier, and salary/offer questions close the round.

modules.title: Technical Interview Preparation
modules.intro: Technical interview prep (fresher level) is the meta-skill module — how to handle the interview itself. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with approaching coding problems and explaining your thought process (the two skills that matter most), then whiteboard coding tips. Mock interview approach and handling unknown questions follow at the practice tier, then common fresher mistakes. Post-interview follow-up and system-design intro questions close the module.

modules.title: Spring Security Basics
modules.intro: Spring Security (fresher level) introduces securing a Spring app. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with authentication vs authorization (the two concerns), then the security config and form-login flow (the default Spring Security path). Method-level security follows at the mechanics tier, then JWT token basics (the stateless model most APIs use). Spring Security interview questions close the module.

modules.title: JVM Internals & Memory Management
modules.intro: JVM memory (fresher level) introduces how Java manages memory. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with JVM architecture (the runtime data areas), then heap vs stack (where objects vs frames live — the distinction every fresher must nail), then garbage collection basics (how the heap gets cleaned). Each topic builds on the memory model the previous one establishes.

modules.title: Spring Boot Testing
modules.intro: Spring testing (fresher level) introduces testing Spring applications. This module is an elevation arc: it opens with unit vs integration testing (the distinction and the Spring context boundary), then the @SpringBootTest annotation (the integration-test workhorse), then @WebMvcTest (the slice test for controllers). Each topic builds the testing-strategy picture a fresher needs.
